newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures seen building on recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures seen building on recent gains.

text.p: Bund futures were expected to build on last week's gains on Monday, receiving continued support from U.S. Treasuries and expectations that monetary union will start on time in 1999.
The DTB September Bund future was up 22 basis points in early trade to 101.76, topping Friday's high of 101.73. The contract had climbed 16 basis points on Friday to 101.55.

Traders said the major focus is the European Union summit in Amsterdam where ministers are trying to reach an agreement on French demands for new meausres to promote growth and jobs alongside the stability pact limiting budget deficits.
Traders said comments from officials attending the conference suggest that a deal is near and the new French government will not get in the way of the EMU launch.

In advance of any news from Amsterdam, traders said they expected the futures contract to trade roughly between 101.40 and 101.80, with any sustained break above that range paving the way toward 102.00.
Traders said market sentiment is clearly bullish and Bunds should push higher as long as Treasuries do not reverse what were strong gains last week.
"Short-term conditions still appear bullish even if we do have more consolidation immediately ahead," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said in a market commentary.
The investment house said heavy selling in the Bobl contract on Friday suggested that outperfomrance in the five-year sector of the yield curve has come to an end.
After flattening much of last week, the yield curve was steady on Monday morning at 227 basis points.
Bunds were also relatively steady against Treasuries this morning with the spread at 83 basis points, down one basis point from Friday.
